items.label: Elamipretide × primary mitochondrial diseases
items.rationale: RCT-level evidence exists but is unreadable: the phase-3 (NCT05162768, n=102) and phase-4 (NCT07531251, n=48) placebo-controlled trials have no posted efficacy results, and registry data (NCT05168774) cannot raise evidence quality per the rubric. Effect_direction is capped at 3 for negative/inconclusive late-stage evidence: the systematic trial survey reports 'several well-designed late-stage trials have yielded negative or inconclusive outcomes' (42361626) and the meta-analysis of antioxidant/metabolic therapies found 'largely negative or mixed results' (42630618); the only human efficacy-like signal is a single uncontrolled case report (LVEF 20%→50%, Ross class IV→I, non-significant, no comparator; 42415111). Pipeline momentum is the strongest in the set: regulatory authorizations (42361626), two FDA approvals in one year (42229401), first indication for muscle strength in Barth syndrome (42359884), and active phase-1/3/4 trials (NCT05168774, NCT05162768, NCT07531251). Unmet need remains high because SOC is supportive care without a broadly approved disease-modifying therapy. Translatability is moderate: parenteral peptide, safety accumulated in RCTs (NCT05162768) but not an oral small molecule.

items.label: MitoQ × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Positive significant preclinical signal in a rat MI model — improved hemodynamics and reduced total/mitochondrial superoxide (42432986) — but the MitoQ-specific meta-analysis reports unclear oxidative-stress outcomes (42495453) and the only registered human trial (8-week placebo-controlled RCT, n=31; NCT05561556) has no posted results, so evidence quality stays preclinical-grade. Effect direction 5 reflects consistent animal benefit with unclear human data and no negative RCT signal. Pipeline momentum is moderate: one active registered RCT (NCT05561556) plus a 2026 meta (42495453). Unmet need is partial because CHF has robust GDMT (ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blockers, MRA, SGLT2i). MitoQ is an oral small molecule with supplement-grade safety, giving high translatability.

items.label: Mitochondria-targeted agents (class) × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: The only statistically significant patient-relevant signal in the record set: a 2026 meta-analysis of mitochondria-targeted agents reports LVEF SMD 0.42 vs control (95% CI 0.31–0.53), NYHA improvement RR 2.38 (1.48–3.84), all-cause mortality RR 0.62 (0.47–0.82) and HF hospitalizations RR 0.60 (0.42–0.85), all p<0.05 (42440741) — consistent benefit across outcomes justifies high component scores. However, constituent trials are small placebo-controlled phase-2 RCTs with no GDMT comparator, so superiority over SOC is unproven, and the direction rests on a single ref_id: the thin-evidence rule caps the total at 4.0 (uncapped weighted sum 6.0). Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (42440741).

items.label: AAV2-ND6 allotopic gene therapy × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
items.rationale: Preclinical-only: restored visual function and attenuated disease progression in ND6P25L mice, with robust sustained retinal/optic-nerve expression and no apparent systemic toxicity (42709484) — a strong single-model signal, but no human dosing data, so effect direction reflects preclinical benefit only and evidence quality stays low. No registered human trial for this specific vector exists in the record set (LHON pipeline momentum comes from other programs: NCT07406854, NCT05293626, NCT05820152, NCT06088992). Unmet need is high: idebenone (SOC) is not curative. Translatability is limited by AAV delivery with no human safety data yet (42709484). Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (42709484); total capped from 4.5 to 4.0.

items.label: Calhex231 × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Single randomized preclinical rat MI study: significant reversal of LVEDD dilation, reduced EF impairment, and decreased myocardial fibrosis, plus in vitro macrophage assays (42748783). Positive direction across three outcomes but entirely preclinical with no human data, so evidence quality is low. No registered human trial → minimal pipeline momentum. Unmet need partial (GDMT is SOC but post-MI remodeling/fibrosis remain undertreated). Small-molecule class with oral dosing feasibility in rodents (42748783) gives moderate-high translatability. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (42748783); total capped from 4.4 to 4.0.

items.label: NR + exercise training × AYA HCT survivors
items.rationale: Well-designed randomized placebo-controlled 2×2 factorial phase-2 RCT (n=80) registered for muscle strength, muscle mass, OXPHOS capacity and VO2max (NCT05194397) — good design and active registration, but no posted results, so evidence_quality and effect_direction stay at baseline (all outcomes coded unclear). Unmet need high: no SOC listed for this population in the map. Oral NR plus exercise is highly translatable and safe. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT05194397); total capped from 4.1 to 4.0.

items.label: MitoQ × amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
items.rationale: Single non-randomized phase-2 pilot (n=50, individualized supplement arms) registered to determine whether MitoQ slows ALS progression, with no posted results (NCT06429059) — momentum comes from the registry only; no effect data exist. Unmet need high: ALS lacks a broadly effective disease-modifying standard. MitoQ is an oral supplement with an established safety record. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT06429059); weighted sum 3.8 is below the thin-evidence cap.

items.label: Nicotinamide riboside × primary mitochondrial diseases
items.rationale: Single phase-2 clinical trial (n=34) of NR for adult-onset mitochondrial myopathy with results 'not reported' (NCT05590468) — momentum only; no effect estimates exist. Unmet need high: SOC for PMD is supportive care with no broadly approved disease-modifying therapy. NR is an oral vitamin B3 derivative with nutraceutical-grade safety. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT05590468); weighted sum 3.8 is below the thin-evidence cap.

items.label: Nicotinamide riboside × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Single registered phase-2 interventional study (n=60) of nicotinamide riboside in cancer-therapy-related cardiac dysfunction, skeletal muscle injury and functional capacity, with no posted results (NCT05732051) — no effect signal; registry data cannot raise evidence quality. Unmet need partial: GDMT is the established SOC for CHF. NR is an oral, safe B3 derivative → high translatability. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT05732051); weighted sum 3.8 is below the thin-evidence cap.

items.label: NAMPT activation (P7C3) × chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Single preclinical study (rat ischemia/reperfusion; H9C2 hypoxia/reoxygenation) showing improved cardiac function, reduced infarct size and ROS, and preserved mitochondrial membrane potential — consistently positive direction but all non-significant and preclinical (42735786). No human trials registered → minimal pipeline momentum. Unmet need partial (GDMT is SOC). P7C3 is a small molecule dosed in rodents (42735786), with human safety not established. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (42735786); weighted sum 3.8 is below the thin-evidence cap.

items.label: MitoQ × primary mitochondrial diseases
items.rationale: The meta-analysis of non-specific antioxidant and metabolic therapies in PMD found 'largely negative or mixed results' in clinical trials (42630618) — no positive human signal, so effect direction is neutral-to-negative. No registered MitoQ-PMD trial exists in the record set (only research-level activity, 42630618), so pipeline momentum is minimal. Unmet need high (supportive-care SOC). MitoQ is an oral small molecule with established supplement-grade safety. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (42630618); weighted sum 3.5 is below the thin-evidence cap.

items.label: NR082 × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
items.rationale: The largest LHON program in the record set: a phase-3 RCT (n=95; NCT07406854) and a phase-2 trial (n=12; NCT05293626) are both registered without posted visual-acuity or safety results, so per the registry-only rule momentum is credited but evidence quality and effect direction stay at baseline. Unmet need high: idebenone (SOC) is not curative and no trial is head-to-head against it. AAV gene-therapy delivery/safety remains unresolved in humans (NCT07406854, NCT05293626). Two distinct ref_ids → not thin.

items.label: OPGx-RDH12-1001 × LCA-IRD
items.rationale: First-in-human phase 1b/2a dose-escalation gene-therapy trial (n=10) evaluating safety and effectiveness at two dose levels with no results reported (NCT07681778) — momentum only; no effect data. Unmet need very high: LCA has no disease-modifying standard of care. Gene-therapy translatability limited to FIH safety (NCT07681778). Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT07681778); weighted sum 3.2 is below the thin-evidence cap.

items.label: HG004 gene therapy × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
items.rationale: Single early-phase-1 safety/efficacy cohort (n=9) with no posted results (NCT06088992) — registry momentum only, no effect signal, and gene-therapy delivery/safety unresolved in humans. Unmet need high (idebenone-only SOC). Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT06088992). Outsider: no human efficacy signal of any kind.

items.label: NFS-02 gene therapy × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
items.rationale: Single single-arm phase 1/2 trial (n=11) with safety, tolerability and visual acuity endpoints all unposted (NCT05820152) — momentum only, no effect signal; no comparator against idebenone. Unmet need high (idebenone-only SOC). Gene-therapy translatability unresolved (NCT05820152). Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (NCT05820152). Outsider: single unblinded cohort, no efficacy readout.

items.label: Antioxidant/redox therapies (NAC, elamipretide) × retinitis pigmentosa
items.rationale: A review only: it proposes extracellular mtDNA as a candidate biomarker of disease activity and pharmacodynamic endpoint, never previously quantified in RP ocular fluids (42792149) — no efficacy data and no registered trials in the record set, hence zero pipeline momentum. Unmet need high: RP has no broadly applicable disease-modifying standard. Translatability mixed: NAC is oral but elamipretide is parenteral (42792149). Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (42792149). Outsider: biomarker-concept stage only.

items.label: MitoQ × stress-related disorders
items.rationale: A single narrative review lists mitoquinone mesylate among mitochondria-targeted therapeutic strategies for emotional stress with an empty, non-significant, unclear outcome (41594657) — no effect estimates, no trials, no pipeline. Unmet need moderate (no SOC listed for this population, but severity lower than the listed monogenic diseases). MitoQ is an oral, safe small molecule. Thin evidence base: 1 ref_id (41594657). Lowest-scoring direction in the set.

outsiders: HG004 gene therapy × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (2.9): single early phase-1 cohort (n=9) with no posted safety/efficacy results (NCT06088992); gene-therapy delivery unresolved; zero human efficacy signal.
NFS-02 gene therapy × Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (2.9): single single-arm phase 1/2 (n=11) with unposted visual-acuity results and no idebenone comparator (NCT05820152).
Antioxidant/redox therapies (NAC, elamipretide) × retinitis pigmentosa (2.6): only a review proposing a never-quantified mtDNA biomarker (42792149); no efficacy data and no registered trials.
MitoQ × stress-related disorders (2.6): single narrative review with an empty, unclear outcome (41594657); no trials, no pipeline, no human effect estimate.
caveats: No direction reaches the leader threshold (total >= 6): top score is 4.8 (elamipretide × primary mitochondrial diseases) — 'no convincing leaders yet'.

All 14 registered trials in the record set lack posted results (coded direction=unclear); per the rubric, registry-only evidence was used to score pipeline_momentum only, never evidence_quality or effect_direction (e.g., NCT05162768, NCT07531251, NCT05561556, NCT07406854, NCT05194397, NCT07681778).

The strongest human signal in the set — the class-level CHF meta-analysis (LVEF SMD 0.42 vs control; mortality RR 0.62; hospitalization RR 0.60; 42440741) — rests on small placebo-controlled phase-2 RCTs with no GDMT comparator and a single ref_id, so its direction is capped at 4.0 by the thin-evidence rule; constituent-trial agents are not enumerated, so the benefit cannot be attributed to any named drug (e.g., MitoQ).

Elamipretide × PMD effect_direction capped at 3: negative/inconclusive late-stage trial outcomes reported in the systematic survey (42361626) plus largely negative/mixed meta-analytic results for antioxidant/metabolic therapies (42630618); no posted phase-3 efficacy dataset exists for elamipretide itself (NCT05162768).

Four single-ref directions had uncapped weighted sums above 4 (class-CHF 6.0, AAV2-ND6×LHON 4.5, Calhex231×CHF 4.4, NR+exercise×AYA-HCT 4.1) and were capped at 4.0; 14 of 17 directions overall rest on a single ref_id and are flagged 'thin evidence base'.

Endpoints are largely surrogate (LVEF, ROS, OXPHOS capacity, mouse visual function); no trial is head-to-head against idebenone (LHON SOC) or GDMT (CHF SOC), so effect versus standard of care remains unquantified.

SOC-map tension: the trial survey and commentary report regulatory authorizations for four PMD therapies (42361626, 42229401), but the SOC map still lists supportive care with no approved disease-modifying therapy; unmet_need scores follow the SOC map, tempered where subtype-specific approvals exist (42359884).

Non-interventional records with no treatment arm were excluded from scoring as directions: 42632451 (m.11778G>A genetic architecture), 42747679 (SIRT3 antifibrotic mechanistic review), 40974057 (single-cell omics methods).
